identity.name: Polyglycerol esters of fatty acids
identity.chemical_class: Mixed polyglycerol fatty-acid esters (non-ionic emulsifier class)

function.mechanism: Amphiphilic esters lower oil-water interfacial tension and stabilize emulsions; specific forms are used to inhibit clouding in edible oils.

adi.basis: EFSA 2017 concluded E475 was not of safety concern at reported uses and that there was no need for a numerical ADI.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA follow-up (2022) maintained the safety conclusion framework while recommending tighter specifications for impurities (toxic elements, erucic acid, 3-MCPD, glycidyl esters).

adi.basis: WHO JECFA database lists ADI 0-25 mg/kg bw and a 2024 reaffirmation comment.

concerns.summary: EFSA 2022 identified specification-level concerns and recommended lower maximum limits or added limits for arsenic, lead, mercury, cadmium, erucic acid, 3-MCPD, and glycidyl esters.
In vitro studies reported immune-cell or macrophage functional effects at high concentrations (around or above 1 mg/mL), with lower concentrations reported as uncritical in the specific test systems.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2017 reported no genotoxic potential from available data and no adverse effects in short-term, subchronic, or chronic studies at tested doses.
EFSA 2017 reported no adverse findings in a limited volunteer study up to 300 mg/kg bw/day for 3 weeks.
No IARC classification entry for E475/polyglycerol esters of fatty acids was identified in the checked IARC classification resources.

populations: children (higher relative exposure than adults in EFSA scenarios)
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA non-brand-loyal scenario reported highest child P95 exposure of 6.4 mg/kg bw/day, below 25 mg/kg bw/day; uncertainty remains due limited use-level data coverage in some categories.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory assessments remain favorable (EFSA no numerical ADI needed at reported uses; JECFA ADI 0-25 mg/kg bw; FDA permitted use in 21 CFR 172.854). Available concerns are mainly impurity/specification management and high-concentration in vitro effects, without strong evidence of harm at normal dietary use levels.
key_factors: EU and US approvals with defined conditions
EFSA 2017 no safety concern at reported uses and no need for numerical ADI
JECFA ADI 0-25 mg/kg bw reaffirmed in 2024 database entry
Limited recent human direct toxicity evidence
